blocks.text: The Unvoiced knob adjusts the volume of an additional noise generator, which is used to resynthesize portions of the modulator signal that are pitchless, such as ”f” and ”s” sounds.
blocks.raw_html: The Unvoiced knob adjusts the volume of an additional noise generator, which is used to resynthesize portions of the modulator signal that are pitchless, such as ”f” and ”s” sounds.

blocks.text: Sens. sets the sensitivity of the unvoiced detection algorithm. At 100%, the unvoiced noise generator is always on. At 0%, only the main carrier source is used. The Fast/Slow switch adjusts how quickly Vocoder switches between unvoiced and voiced detection.
blocks.raw_html: Sens. sets the sensitivity of the unvoiced detection algorithm. At 100%, the unvoiced noise generator is always on. At 0%, only the main carrier source is used. The Fast/Slow switch adjusts how quickly Vocoder switches between unvoiced and voiced detection.

blocks.text: Vocoder’s large central area shows the levels of the individual band-pass filters. Clicking within this display allows you to attenuate these levels.
blocks.raw_html: Vocoder’s large central area shows the levels of the individual band-pass filters. Clicking within this display allows you to attenuate these levels.

blocks.text: The Bands chooser sets the number of filters that will be used. Using more bands results in a more accurate analysis of the modulator’s frequency content, but requires more CPU.
blocks.raw_html: The Bands chooser sets the number of filters that will be used. Using more bands results in a more accurate analysis of the modulator’s frequency content, but requires more CPU.

blocks.text: The Range sliders adjust the frequency range over which the band-pass filters will operate. For most sources, a fairly large range works well, but you may want to adjust the outer limits if the sound becomes too piercing or bassy. The BW control sets the bandwidth of the filters. At low percentages, each filter approaches a single frequency. As you increase the bandwidth, you increase the overlap of the filter bands. A bandwidth of 100% is the most accurate, but higher or lower settings can create interesting effects.
blocks.raw_html: The Range sliders adjust the frequency range over which the band-pass filters will operate. For most sources, a fairly large range works well, but you may want to adjust the outer limits if the sound becomes too piercing or bassy. The BW control sets the bandwidth of the filters. At low percentages, each filter approaches a single frequency. As you increase the bandwidth, you increase the overlap of the filter bands. A bandwidth of 100% is the most accurate, but higher or lower settings can create interesting effects.

blocks.text: The Precise/Retro switch toggles between two types of filter behavior. In Precise mode, all filters have the same gain and bandwidth. In Retro mode, bands become narrower and louder at higher frequencies.
blocks.raw_html: The Precise/Retro switch toggles between two types of filter behavior. In Precise mode, all filters have the same gain and bandwidth. In Retro mode, bands become narrower and louder at higher frequencies.

blocks.text: Gate sets a threshold for the filterbank. Any bands whose levels are below the threshold will be silent.
blocks.raw_html: Gate sets a threshold for the filterbank. Any bands whose levels are below the threshold will be silent.

blocks.text: The Level slider boosts or cuts Vocoder’s output.
blocks.raw_html: The Level slider boosts or cuts Vocoder’s output.

blocks.text: Depth sets how much of the modulator’s amplitude envelope is applied to the carrier’s signal. At 0%, the modulator’s envelope is discarded. At 200%, only high amplitude peaks will be used. 100% results in ”classic” vocoding.
blocks.raw_html: Depth sets how much of the modulator’s amplitude envelope is applied to the carrier’s signal. At 0%, the modulator’s envelope is discarded. At 200%, only high amplitude peaks will be used. 100% results in ”classic” vocoding.

blocks.text: The Attack and Release controls set how quickly Vocoder responds to amplitude changes in the modulator signal. Very fast times preserve the transients of the modulator, but can cause distortion artifacts.
blocks.raw_html: The Attack and Release controls set how quickly Vocoder responds to amplitude changes in the modulator signal. Very fast times preserve the transients of the modulator, but can cause distortion artifacts.

blocks.text: The Mono/Stereo switches determine how many channels are used for the carrier and modulator. In Mono mode, both the carrier and modulator are treated as mono sources. Stereo uses a mono modulator but processes the carrier in stereo. L/R processes both the carrier and modulator signals in stereo.
blocks.raw_html: The Mono/Stereo switches determine how many channels are used for the carrier and modulator. In Mono mode, both the carrier and modulator are treated as mono sources. Stereo uses a mono modulator but processes the carrier in stereo. L/R processes both the carrier and modulator signals in stereo.

blocks.text: The frequencies of the carrier’s filterbank can be shifted up or down via the Formant knob. With voice as the modulator, small Formant changes can alter the apparent gender of the source.
blocks.raw_html: The frequencies of the carrier’s filterbank can be shifted up or down via the Formant knob. With voice as the modulator, small Formant changes can alter the apparent gender of the source.

blocks.text: The Dry/Wet control adjusts the balance between the processed and dry signals.
blocks.raw_html: The Dry/Wet control adjusts the balance between the processed and dry signals.

blocks.text: 29.42.1 Vocoder Tips
blocks.raw_html: 29.42.1 Vocoder Tips

blocks.text: This section explains how to set up the most common Vocoder applications.
blocks.raw_html: This section explains how to set up the most common Vocoder applications.

blocks.text: 29.42.1.1 Singing Synthesizer
blocks.raw_html: 29.42.1.1 Singing Synthesizer

blocks.text: The classic vocoder application is the ”singing synthesizer.” To set this up in Live:
blocks.raw_html: The classic vocoder application is the ”singing synthesizer.” To set this up in Live:

blocks.text: Insert Vocoder in the track that contains your vocal material. You can either use a clip that contains a prerecorded voice clip or, to process a live vocal signal, connect a microphone to a channel on your audio hardware and choose this as the input source for the track.
blocks.raw_html: • Insert Vocoder in the track that contains your vocal material. You can either use a clip that contains a prerecorded voice clip or, to process a live vocal signal, connect a microphone to a channel on your audio hardware and choose this as the input source for the track.

blocks.text: Insert a synthesizer such as Analog in another track. Again, you can either create a MIDI clip to drive this synthesizer or play it live.
blocks.raw_html: • Insert a synthesizer such as Analog in another track. Again, you can either create a MIDI clip to drive this synthesizer or play it live.

blocks.text: Set the vocoder’s Carrier chooser to External.
blocks.raw_html: • Set the vocoder’s Carrier chooser to External.

blocks.text: Select the synthesizer track in the vocoder’s Audio From choosers. (For best results, choose Post FX in the bottom chooser.)
blocks.raw_html: • Select the synthesizer track in the vocoder’s Audio From choosers. (For best results, choose Post FX in the bottom chooser.)

blocks.text: If you’re creating your synthesizer and vocal material in real time, make sure the Arm button is enabled on both tracks.
blocks.raw_html: • If you’re creating your synthesizer and vocal material in real time, make sure the Arm button is enabled on both tracks.

blocks.text: Play the synthesizer as you speak into the microphone. You’ll hear the rhythm of your speech, but with the timbral character and frequencies of the synthesizer. To hear the vocoded signal alone, solo the voice track so that the ”normal” synthesizer track is muted.
blocks.raw_html: • Play the synthesizer as you speak into the microphone. You’ll hear the rhythm of your speech, but with the timbral character and frequencies of the synthesizer. To hear the vocoded signal alone, solo the voice track so that the ”normal” synthesizer track is muted.

blocks.text: Note: you’ll generally get the best results if your synthesizer sound is bright and rich in harmonics. Try sawtooth-based patches to improve the intelligibility of the voice. For even more brightness and clarity, try adjusting the Unvoiced control and/or enabling Enhance.
blocks.raw_html: Note: you’ll generally get the best results if your synthesizer sound is bright and rich in harmonics. Try sawtooth-based patches to improve the intelligibility of the voice. For even more brightness and clarity, try adjusting the Unvoiced control and/or enabling Enhance.

blocks.text: 29.42.1.2 Formant Shifter
blocks.raw_html: 29.42.1.2 Formant Shifter

blocks.text: If the Vocoder is set to use the modulator as its own carrier, it can be used as a powerful formant shifter. To do this:
blocks.raw_html: If the Vocoder is set to use the modulator as its own carrier, it can be used as a powerful formant shifter. To do this:

blocks.text: Set the Carrier chooser to Modulator.
blocks.raw_html: • Set the Carrier chooser to Modulator.

blocks.text: Set the Depth to 100%.
blocks.raw_html: • Set the Depth to 100%.

blocks.text: Enable Enhance.
blocks.raw_html: • Enable Enhance.

blocks.text: Now experiment with different settings of the Formant knob to alter the character of the source. For even more sound-sculpting possibilities, try adjusting the various filterbank parameters as well.
blocks.raw_html: Now experiment with different settings of the Formant knob to alter the character of the source. For even more sound-sculpting possibilities, try adjusting the various filterbank parameters as well.

owner_requirements.contract: Panning uses two LFOs to alternate channel amplitudes; Tremolo uses one amplitude LFO. Mode changes waveform/control presentation and position versus amplitude visualization.
Waveform choices are Sine, Triangle, Shark Tooth, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square, Random, Wander and S&H.
Time modes are Rate, Time, Synced, Dotted, Triplet and 16th. Rate exposes Freq in Hz; Time exposes Time in ms with 100 ms to 200 s period; beat modes expose Rate in beat divisions.
Stereo Offset offers Phase or Spin, but Random, Wander and S&H permit Phase only. Phase offsets channel LFOs in degrees; 180 degrees is opposite phase; Spin progressively diverges them by percentage.
Phase Offset is available for beat-division Time modes and offsets LFO cycle start relative to grid; with Random, Wander or S&H it functions as stereo width.
Invert flips LFO polarity. Shape changes Panning overlap/transition and Tremolo rounded versus angular peaks; ramp extrema with Invert off/on produce gating/pumping.
Tremolo offers Harmonic, alternating high/low modulation around a fixed 600 Hz crossover, and Vintage, adding nonlinear shaping to amplitude modulation.
Amount determines modulation depth; Amount and LFO rate values are shared by Panning and Tremolo rather than independently stored per mode.
Attack Time sets milliseconds to reach maximum modulation after a detected transient; longer values preserve initial transient center/impact before sustained modulation.
Dynamic Frequency Modulation makes louder input increase LFO rate at positive values and decrease it at negative values.

Auto Shift processes monophonic audio. Input Pitch displays note/cents; High/Mid/Bass range LEDs indicate matching input range; range changes affect latency. Input Gain ranges -24 to +24 dB. Live Mode reduces latency with possible onset/rapid-change glitches.

MIDI In shows/hides routing panel; MIDI On activates input and replaces Quantizer with MIDI tab. Source selects a separate MIDI track; Pre FX bypasses its MIDI effects and Post FX/Post Mixer includes them.
Mono uses one correction voice and Glide for overlapping notes. Poly offers maximum counts 2, 4 or 8.
In MIDI mode the processed path only produces sound when notes are received. Dry/Wet mixes original/processed, so dry monitoring must be excluded when testing this condition.

Quantizer follows selected/included scale notes; meter reports cents correction and target note. Correction Strength increases correction; Smooth retains more natural vibrato and smooths transitions with 0-200 ms Smoothing Time. Scale-degree Pitch Shift follows correction.

Use Current Scale follows clip scale, highlights included notes purple and disables Root/Scale choosers. Scale awareness is unavailable with MIDI input; source Scale MIDI effect needs Post FX/Post Mixer to apply.
MIDI tab visualizes received notes and offers Attack 0-1000 ms, Release 0-5 s, Note Latch holding until next Note On, and Pitch Bend Range 0-48 semitones.
Pitch, Formant, Volume and Pan each offer Velocity, Pressure, Mod Wheel, Pitch Bend, Note PB or Slide as modulation sources with dedicated depth.
LFO Reset retriggers phase at note onset. Quantizer onset follows a period of unpitched audio; MIDI onset is start of a new note; indicator changes from Onset to Trigger.

LFO Delay is 0-1.5 s, Attack 0-2 s. Waveforms are Sine, Triangle, Triangle 8, Triangle 16, Saw Up, Saw Down, Rectangle, Random, Random S&H. Rate uses ms or tempo divisions; depths target Pitch/Formant/Volume/Pan.
LFO, semitone/cent Pitch Shift and Formant Shift work without correction. Formant Shift spans -100% to +100%; Formant Follow sets how much formants follow pitch shifting.

Vibrato works with/without correction; Amount is 0-200 cents, Rate 2-15 Hz, Fade In is ms and Natural adds rate/depth variation. Dry/Wet ranges from original at 0% to processed at 100%, with balanced 50%.

Mode chooser selects Chorus, Ensemble or Vibrato; display shows active delay lines. Chorus adds time-modulated delays; Ensemble describes three phase-offset delays; Vibrato emphasizes pitch modulation.
Each mode offers high-pass enable and frequency 20 Hz to 2 kHz; enabled filter reduces modulation below chosen frequency.
Chorus/Ensemble Width sets wet mid/side balance: 0% mono, 100% balanced and 200% sides twice mid level.
Chorus offers Auto or fixed Delay Time and one/two taps. Auto scales delay per tap with modulation amount; fixed delay does not scale with amount.
Vibrato offers channel Offset with opposite LFO phase at 180 degrees and Shape from sine at 0% to triangle at 100%.
Rate is Hz; Amount controls delay-time modulation; Feedback feeds each channel output to input and can produce audible delays after stop; Feedback Invert reverses feedback polarity.
Feedback and Dry/Wet controls are disabled in Vibrato mode.
Output gains processed signal; Warmth adds distortion/filtering; Dry/Wet balances processed/original outside Vibrato.

Phaser/Flanger/Doubler select distinct display/control roles. Phaser offers Notches, Center, Spread and Blend (Center at 0, Spread at 1); Flanger/Doubler offer Time with opposite visualization directions.

Unfold reveals main LFO detail, second LFO, envelope and Safe Bass. Main Freq/Rate is Hz or tempo-sync. Shapes include Sine, Triangle, Saw Up/Down, Rectangle, Random, Random S&H, Triangle Analog/8/16.
Phase changes channel LFO relationship with opposite phase at 180 degrees; Spin detunes the two LFO rates.
Duty Cycle skews the waveform period toward front at +100% or back at -100%, neutral at 0%; it does not affect Random or Random S&H.
LFO2 is triangular, with independent Hz/synced rate. LFO2 Mix 0% selects main only and 100% selects LFO2 only.
Amount affects both LFOs. Feedback returns channel output, supports polarity inversion, and in Doubler can continue as audible delays after stop; high feedback may raise levels quickly.
Envelope modulation requires Env Fol on and nonzero Envelope Amount; negative amount inverts envelope phase. Attack/Release govern rising/falling modulation response.
Safe Bass is a high-pass reducing effect below selected frequency, with 5-3000 Hz range.
Output gains processed signal; Warmth adds distortion/filtering; Dry/Wet balances processed/original.
Pitch mode exposes semitone Coarse and cent Fine transposition; Freq shifts Hz; Ring adds/subtracts the entered Hz frequency to/from input.
Wide inverts Spread for right channel, shifting right down while left shifts up; Wide has no effect at Spread zero.
Pitch offers Window size; Tone cuts high frequencies in delay feedback. Delay enable exposes free or beat-synced time and Feedback; source describes free units as Hertz.

LFO offers Duty Cycle, Phase/Spin and beat-sync Offset. Deterministic shapes allow Phase/Spin; Random uses Phase, Random S&H uses Width. Width endpoints describe LFO channels, not necessarily equal/opposite audio.
LFO choices are Sine, Triangle, Triangle Analog, Triangle 8/16, Saw Up/Down, Rectangle, Random and Random S&H; Rate is Hz or tempo subdivisions and Amount sets modulation.
Env Fol enables input-amplitude modulation; Attack/Release govern rising/falling response. Amount uses semitones in Pitch or Hz in Freq/Ring.
Drive distortion is available only in Ring mode, with amount slider.
Dry/Wet balances original/processed output.
Unfolded Pitch Mode selects Internal (Coarse/Fine) or MIDI (incoming note). MIDI exposes source, Glide in ms and PB range 0-24 semitones.
Internal fixes resonator pitch; MIDI follows external notes. MIDI source/tapping chooses before/after source effects; Mono/Poly selects one or poly voices, with Polyphony 2-16.
Mono MIDI Gate on requires held notes for resonance; off still responds to audio. Gate is always active in Poly. Glide is active only in Mono; PB is 0-24 semitones and MPE reception is supported.

Internal Freq supports Hz or note; Use Current Scale replaces it with SD Shift and follows clip scale or chromatic when no scale active. MIDI Transp spans +/-48 semitones or +/-28 scale degrees. Active tuning makes Freq/Transp use note indices.
Stretch compresses spacing below 0 and expands above; 100% produces odd harmonics. Shift transposes input spectrum +/-48 semitones, distinct from resonator spectrum.
Decay controls resonance persistence; HF/LF Damp affect partials in ranges following current/internal or incoming MIDI pitch.

Modulation modes None, Chorus, Wander and Granular select no modulation, triangle partial modulation, random sawtooth, or random exponential-envelope grains respectively. Mod Rate/Pch. Mod set rate and pitch range.
None applies no modulation; Chorus at Mod Rate zero modulates partial amplitudes only. Pitch modulation is bipolar except Granular's positive grain envelopes.
Spectrogram displays dry yellow/wet blue and can hide. Harmonics sets count shared evenly across poly voices; Quantize snaps harmonics to active scale/tuning or chromatic fallback.
Input Send gains processed signal with limiter-use LED; Unison adds detuned partial copies and Uni. Amt sets detuning. Wander/Granular modulate voices independently. Dry/Wet balances paths.
Freezer and Delay have separate On controls; Frz > Dly/Dly > Frz selects processing order. Generic freezer-feeds-delay prose is read in Frz > Dly context, not as unconditional order.
Spectrogram dry/wet is yellow/blue and hideable. Zero Dry Signal Latency avoids aligning dry to processed output. Lower Resolution reduces latency at fidelity cost.
Freezer must be On and Freeze toggled for effect in both Manual/Retrigger. Manual Freeze captures audio with Fade In/Fade Out in ms.
Retrigger offers Onsets with Sensitivity 0-100% (lowest/highest) or Sync with Interval in ms or beat time.
Retrigger Crossfade fades new freeze in while old/dry fades out; X-Fade is relative to interval. Envelope uses ms Fade In/Out and stacks up to eight simultaneous freezes.
Delay Time modes are Time (ms), Notes (beat divisions), 16th, 16th Triplet and 16th Dotted (count of selected sixteenths).
Delay Feedback returns output to input; Shift adds frequency shift per successive delay; Stereo adjusts Tilt/Spray width. Delay Dry/Wet affects only Delay section.
Positive Tilt delays high frequencies more, negative delays low more; Spray randomizes frequency delay times in its range; positive/negative Mask limits Tilt/Spray to high/low frequencies.
Input Send sets input gain; global Dry/Wet balances whole processed/dry device, separate from Delay Dry/Wet.

Device track input is modulator; carrier choices are Noise, External, Modulator and Pitch Tracking. Noise X/Y changes downsampling/density; External selects internal audio routing; Modulator uses same input for both roles.

Pitch Tracking is monophonic, bounded by High/Low and selectable sawtooth/three pulse shapes with coarse Pitch. It updates only on clear pitch and holds last detected pitch otherwise; reset/grouping may change sound.
Enhance normalizes carrier spectrum/dynamics for brightness; Unvoiced adds noise. Sens 100% keeps unvoiced generator on, 0% uses main carrier only; Fast/Slow changes detection switching.
Band display allows attenuation; Bands selects filter count; Range limits filter frequencies; BW controls overlap. Precise has equal gain/bandwidth; Retro narrows/raises higher bands.

Gate silences below-threshold filter bands; Level sets output gain. Depth 0% discards modulator envelope, 100% classic vocoding, 200% uses high-amplitude peaks. Attack/Release govern amplitude response.
Channel modes are Mono (both mono), Stereo (mono modulator/stereo carrier) and L/R (both stereo).
Formant shifts carrier filterbank frequencies; Dry/Wet balances modulator original and processed result.

External vocoding uses vocal/modulator track and separate synthesizer carrier track selected in Audio From; Post FX is recommended. Live-input example arms both tracks; soloing voice track isolates documented vocoded result.
Interval ranges 1/32 to 4 Bars and is tempo-relative; Offset shifts capture forward. At Interval 1 Bar, Offset 8/16 selects third beat in a four-beat-bar example.
Chance 100% always repeats at requested Interval/Offset; 0% never repeats.

Gate sets total repeat span in sixteenths; Grid sets slice size. Gate 4/16 spans one beat. Repeat overrides automatic timing/chance/gate and captures/repeats until disabled. No Triplets makes grid binary.
Variation 0 fixes Grid; greater values vary it. Variation modes Trigger, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 and Auto schedule changes at trigger, periodic intervals or each repetition.
Pitch lowers repeats by resampling and lengthens segments without recompression; Pitch Decay lowers each successive slice.
Combined low/high-pass filter has enable, center frequency and passed-band width.
Mix passes original and adds repeats; Insert mutes original only during repeats; Gate passes only repeats.
Volume sets output level and Decay fades repetitions.

Record captures and overwrites existing loop; Overdub adds layers at original length; Play plays without new recording; Stop halts playback. Display is red recording, then position/length in bars/beats. Running Set uses selected quantization; stopped Set acts immediately.
Clear during Overdub with running global transport empties buffer but preserves tempo/length; other modes reset tempo/length.
Looper Undo removes material since latest Overdub enable, preserving original and earlier overdub passes; Redo restores removed pass.
Multi-Purpose single click: empty to Record; Record/Overdub/Stopped to Play; Play to Overdub. Double click stops Play/Overdub. Two-second hold in Play invokes Undo/Redo; hold stopped clears.
Multi-Purpose button supports MIDI-foot-switch mapping through MIDI Map Mode, clicking control, pressing switch then exiting mapping.
Tempo Control None decouples internal/global tempo; Follow changes playback speed to global tempo; Set & Follow sets global tempo from recorded material then follows later global changes.

With Set running, x bars records until another transport button; fixed bars stops at chosen length into Play/Overdub. With Set stopped, x bars guesses tempo at Overdub/Play/Stop, while fixed bars fits recording into chosen bars.

Song Control None leaves global transport; Start Song starts global on entering Play/Overdub but Stop leaves it; Start & Stop Song also stops global. Start via Looper adjusts connected Link apps' phrase position.
x2 duplicates existing buffer and doubles length; /2 retains currently playing half and discards the other half.
Drag me exports buffer to browser/track as file/clip with Re-Pitch Warp default; dragging audio file into Drag me replaces buffer and allows later overdubs.

Speed changes playback speed/pitch; octave arrows double/halve speed and are quantized. Reverse plays previous audio backwards; overdubs made reversed play forward then reverse when Reverse is disabled; Reverse is quantized.
Feedback acts only in Overdub and changes next repetition: 100% retains old level, 50% halves each pass. Play repetitions keep level regardless of Feedback.
Input -> Output options: Always; Never; Rec/OVR (Record/Overdub); Rec/OVR/Stop (all except Play). These govern input monitoring independently of stored-loop playback.
Looper can source and receive internal audio through Insert-Looper: route another track from/to Looper, select Insert-Looper taps, Monitor In and use Overdub for processed feedback layers.

common-setup.set: valid, editable, test-owned Set; reset per independent trial
common-setup.signal_path: isolated enabled device in active track/chain; route named input/MIDI source into it, with monitoring active when needed; explicit 4/4, 120 BPM and 48 kHz chosen as authored setups, not product limits
common-setup.neutralization: disable unrelated automation, mapping, randomization and effects except when named; set gain and wet output nonzero/unmuted; all values used as interior controls must first be admitted by target UI
common-setup.references: use owned disposable copies for destructive/replacement/malformed cases; never change immutable source artifacts

positive-signal-guard.enabled: tested control/section enabled, correct mode, active routing and explicit nonzero amount/depth/send/feedback when testing its influence
positive-signal-guard.baseline: first demonstrate the relevant wet path responds to the test stimulus in a paired positive case; no effect caused by disabled control, zero amount, silence, missing notes, muted channel or dry-only output is evidence
positive-signal-guard.negative_cases: documented zero/disabled exception uses separate nonzero/enabled positive baseline, changes only the targeted setting, and leaves expected signal/comparator null unless independently supplied
positive-signal-guard.stereo: use equal samples in both channels only when dual-mono is specified; LFO channel equality is never generalized to audio equality from distinct stereo inputs
positive-signal-guard.random: no seed, distribution, sequence matching or expectation of identical repeated output is asserted
positive-signal-guard.safety: test-owned bounded low-amplitude source; high-feedback stability is not a grade or a claim

authored_audio.dual_mono: four seconds; left=right=0.125*sin(2*pi*440*t); 48000 frames/s; silence before/after; this formula defines analyst input only
authored_audio.amplitude_steps: 440 Hz dual-mono tone, amplitude 0.03125 for first two seconds, 0.125 next two; separate silence/held-tone segments for onset tests
authored_audio.broadband: owned deterministic multitone 60, 440, 880 and 2400 Hz, each amplitude 0.025; finite 200 ms bursts at 0,1,2,3 seconds; intended bands must be confirmed active in target
authored_audio.phrases: distinct analyst-owned A/B/C segments of 440/660/880 Hz, one 4/4 bar each at 120 BPM; loop orientation/content identifiers, not a measured resampling oracle

authored_midi.events: Use explicit note-on/off pairs with admitted channel/note/velocity in a valid editable source MIDI clip. Single-note A then overlapping B; for voice-boundary cases use distinct held notes up to named voice count then one extra. Release all notes between trials.
authored_midi.limitations: No MIDI byte codec, pitch-frequency mapping, voice allocation, stealing or ordering is supplied by this recipe.

assessments.quote: 29.3 Auto Pan-Tremolo
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: Exact source heading/ancestry only; no behavioral input/action/output or completion credit.

assessments.quote: Auto Pan-Tremolo uses LFO modulation to affect the input signal’s stereo position or amplitude to create automatic panning, tremolo, and gating effects.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: General automatic panning/tremolo/gating role; AP001/006 actual mode/invert trials are subsets, not an amplitude kernel.

assessments.quote: There are two modes available: Panning and Tremolo. In Panning mode, two LFOs modulate the placement of the input signal within the stereo panorama by alternating its amplitude between the left and right channels. In Tremolo mode, a single LFO modulates the signal’s amplitude to create variation in volume. Use the respective toggles to switch between modes. The LFO waveform and controls in the display update depending on which mode is selected to reflect its corresponding properties.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP001 actually switches BOTH Panning/Tremolo and back; mode/display role represented, not private oscillator count enforcement.

assessments.quote: The real-time visualization below the LFO waveform shows the current stereo position in Panning mode or the current amplitude level in Tremolo mode. This makes it easy to see at a glance how the input signal is moving across the left and right channels or how its amplitude is fluctuating.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP001 observes selected display role; current-input movement is not separately driven or checked as audio truth.

assessments.quote: Use the Waveform drop-down to select an LFO shape: Sine, Triangle, Shark Tooth, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square, Random, Wander, and S&H (Sample and Hold).
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP002 actually selects all nine named waves; no sampled waveform or RNG sequence follows.

assessments.quote: Select one of the available Time modes to determine the rate of the LFO: Rate, Time, Synced, Dotted, Triplet, or 16th. Once selected, the corresponding modulation rate control below the drop-down updates to reflect the value associated with that mode. For example, in Time mode, you can set the period of the LFO anywhere from 100 milliseconds to 200 seconds, which is useful for creating long modulation cycles.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP003 actually selects all six Time modes and documented Time endpoints; no beat/sample conversion or rounding follows.

assessments.quote: You can choose between two Stereo Offset modes: Phase and Spin. In Phase mode, the LFO waveforms for the left and right channels can be offset by a set number of degrees. At 180°, the LFOs are perfectly out of phase so that when one LFO reaches its peak value, the other is at its minimum. In Spin mode, the left and right channels diverge progressively based on the set percentage. This adds a subtle asymmetry between the two channels. Note that only Phase mode is available when using the Random, Wander, and S&H waveforms.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP004 tests Sine/Spin then three random-based eligibility exceptions. It does NOT actually adjust Phase180 or nonzero Spin to compare channel relationships.

assessments.quote: When using any of the beat-division-based Time modes (Synced, Triplet, Dotted, or 16th), the Phase Offset control becomes available and can be used to shift the starting point of each LFO channel within its cycle relative to the beat grid. This is useful for offsetting the modulation so that it begins slightly before or after the beat.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP005 selects beat mode/Random and inspects Offset; explicit Offset edits in each beat mode are absent.

assessments.quote: When using the Random, Wander, or S&H waveforms, Phase Offset functions as a stereo width control and can be used to introduce variation between the channels.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP005 preserves random width role without proving free-mode eligibility; no random stereo correlation oracle.

assessments.quote: Use the Invert toggle to flip the polarity of the LFO. When enabled, the positive and negative values of the waveform are swapped, which effectively turns the waveform upside down. In Panning mode, for example, inverting the Saw Up waveform creates a Saw Down waveform. In Tremolo mode, the peaks of the waveform become the valleys and vice versa. When using ramp-shaped waveforms, enabling Invert produces a ducking effect, while disabling it creates a gating effect.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP006 actually varies Invert with a ramp-compatible setting and nonzero Amount; no inversion sample law.

assessments.quote: Tremolo mode includes two additional options that can be enabled to influence the behavior of the LFO modulation: Harmonic and Vintage.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP007 actually enables Harmonic and separately Vintage in Tremolo; selection is real, effect remains U.

assessments.quote: With Harmonic enabled, the high and low frequencies are modulated in an alternating pattern rather than in parallel. A fixed crossover of 600 Hz splits the signal into two frequency bands.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP007 uses components on BOTH sides of600Hz; confirm BOTH independently productive before band-loss contrasts; no crossover curve.

assessments.quote: With Vintage enabled, the signal’s amplitude is modulated by the LFO as well as shaped by a non-linear curve, which adds warmth and grit to the tremolo effect.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP007 separate Vintage trial retains nonlinear adjective as source context, not transfer function.

assessments.quote: Below the display are controls for adjusting the LFO’s amount, rate, shape, attack, and response to the input signal’s level.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: Summary of amount/rate/shape/attack/level response; following paragraphs carry bounded predicates, not a new control family.

assessments.quote: Use the Amount control to set how much LFO modulation is applied to the incoming signal.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP008 edits Amount/rate and carries values across modes; actual Amount influence comparison is not established by displayed values.

assessments.quote: The LFO rate can be set using the control to the right of the Amount control. The name and unit of this control change depending on the selected Time mode. For example, the control appears as Freq when Rate is selected and the value is set in hertz (Hz). In Time mode, the control appears as Time and the value is set in milliseconds (ms). In the Synced, Triplet, Dotted, and 16th modes, the control appears as Rate and the value is set in beat divisions.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP003 actual mode/unit endpoint trial is a true subset; Hz/ms/beat labels do not define codec.

assessments.quote: Note that the values for the Amount control and the LFO rate are shared between the Panning and Tremolo modes and cannot be set independently.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP008 actually switches back after two admissible values; shared-value role represented, constructor state unknown.

assessments.quote: The Shape control affects the LFO waveform differently in each mode. In Panning mode, positive Shape values push each waveform toward its upper and lower limits. This shortens the overlap between the LFOs so that the transition from one channel to the next happens more abruptly. In Tremolo mode, positive values gradually expand the waveform to create rounded peaks, while negative values gradually compress the peaks into an angular shape. At its maximum and minimum values, the Shape control can create ramps for gating effects (with Invert off) and pumping effects (with Invert on).
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP006 varies Shape/Invert but does not explicitly separate positive/negative Shape in BOTH Panning and Tremolo.

assessments.quote: The Attack Time slider sets how long it takes, in milliseconds, to reach the maximum amount of modulation after a transient is detected. A long attack time can be useful for applying the effect only during the sustained portion of the signal while leaving the initial peaks unaffected. In Panning mode, this keeps transients centered in the stereo field, while in Tremolo mode, this helps preserve their impact.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP009 actual transient/sustain and short/long Attack trials exist; no onset threshold or deadline. Separate both-mode transient-centering claims not fully exercised.

assessments.quote: The Dynamic Frequency Modulation slider determines how much the input signal’s level affects the LFO rate. At positive values, louder signals increase the LFO rate, while negative values decrease it.
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.
assessments.assessment: AP010 actual two nonzero levels and positive/negative Dynamic Frequency trials exist; no detector/rate formula.

assessments.quote: 29.4 Auto Shift
assessments.reference_role: Catalog-qualified compared source citations; read the assessment for the actual action subset. Citation presence alone is not sufficiency/coverage.

If Interval is set to ”1 Bar,” for example, and Offset to ”8/16”, material will be captured for repetition once per bar on the third beat (i.e., halfway, or eight-sixteenths of the way, through the bar).

assessments.quote: Spectral Resonator transforms an audio signal by applying tuned resonances to its spectrum. assessments.quote: A vocoder is an effect that combines the frequency information of one audio signal (called the carrier) with the amplitude contour of another audio signal (called the modulator). The modulator source is generally something with a clear rhythmic character such as speech or drums, while the carrier is typically a harmonically-rich synthesizer sound such as a string or pad. The most familiar application of a vocoder is to create ”talking synthesizer” or robotic voice effects.

assessments.quote: Pitch Tracking enables a monophonic oscillator, which tunes itself to the pitch of the modulator. The High and Low sliders allow you to limit the frequency range that the oscillator will attempt to track. Choose from sawtooth or one of three pulse waveforms and adjust the coarse tuning of the oscillator via the Pitch slider. Pitch tracking is particularly effective with monophonic modulator sources such as melodic instruments or voices. Note that the oscillator only updates its frequency when it detects a clear pitch. It then maintains this pitch until it detects a new one. This means that changing the oscillator’s parameters or causing it to reset (when grouping Vocoder’s track, for example) can cause unexpected changes in the sound. With polyphonic material or drums, pitch tracking is generally unpredictable (but can be very interesting.)

assessments.quote: The Range sliders adjust the frequency range over which the band-pass filters will operate. For most sources, a fairly large range works well, but you may want to adjust the outer limits if the sound becomes too piercing or bassy. The BW control sets the bandwidth of the filters.
